full_narration: How can one atomic event decide a whole cat's fate? The clue is a chain: one possible decay can trigger a detector and larger outcome. Schrödinger proposed this thought experiment in 1935. A cat sits inside a sealed box. One radioactive atom may decay. A detector watches for that decay. Its signal can trigger a poison mechanism. Then the cat dies. No decay leaves the cat alive. Quantum theory can describe both atomic possibilities together, called a superposition. The setup links that uncertainty to two cat-sized outcomes. That scale jump was the point. What part feels strangest to you?
